text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: multiple container crashloops observed on runtime-engine-prod-9 (us-west-2). Symptoms: repeated SIGSEGV in inference engine, OOMs preceding segfaults for some pods. Affected selector: app=redwood-runtime, model=rl-7b, cluster=prod-usw2. Auto-scaling triggered, some requests 500ing. Pager sent to SRE.

anya: got the pager, jumping on it now. any initial impact details? cc @miguel @samir

miguel: seeing ~60% of rl-7b replicas CrashLoopBackOff, error logs show "segfault at 0 ip ..." coming from fused kernels. Latency for routed requests to rl-7b up to 4s then 500.

samir: confirmed. From node-level metrics: GPU memory pressure spikes to 100% then OOM kills then segfault. Possibly stale KV cache + long sequences. Also a few nodes flapped (kubelet restart) around same time.

leah: customer-impact: two mid-market customers reported 5xx errors, blocking some real-time features. CS notified them as "investigating"

dev-runtime: pasted recent container logs ->

```
[2026-03-15T14:02:11Z] runtime: vLLM fused-kernel(quant) init
[2026-03-15T14:04:05Z] ERROR sigsegv: signal 11 at 0x7f9ab3c
[2026-03-15T14:04:05Z] backtrace: ... fused_kernel.cu:1427
[2026-03-15T14:04:06Z] OOM: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
```

anya: first mitigation: isolate traffic from rl-7b to fallback model (rl-7b-quant-safe) and scale fallbacks to handle spike. Who can flip routing? @ops-bot?

ops-bot: runbook command to re-route: `redwood route update --name rl-7b --fallback rl-7b-quant-safe --weight 100` (requires approver). @anya, @miguel confirm and I'll execute.

miguel: approve. Execute now.

ops-bot: executed. Confirmed: 100% traffic routed to rl-7b-quant-safe. Observed immediate drop in 500s on frontend. :thumbsup:

samir: good. Next: cordon + drain problematic nodes to stop noisy pods restarting and causing seq cache thrash. Nodes implicated: prod-usw2-n12, prod-usw2-n14. @anya want me to drain?

anya: yes please. Use graceful term 120s to allow in-flight requests to fallback. Also patch daemonset to temporary lower batch size to reduce memory footprint: `kubectl set env ds/redwood-runtime BATCH_SIZE=4`.

samir: draining now ->

```
kubectl cordon prod-usw2-n12
kubectl drain prod-usw2-n12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
kubectl cordon prod-usw2-n14
kubectl drain prod-usw2-n14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
```

leah: CS update: sent note to affected customers: "We've routed traffic to a safe fallback model and are mitigating node restarts — some requests may be slower but should succeed. We'll update within 30m." Customers asked about data loss risk.

dev-runtime: low-latency fix idea: disable fused-kernel path for rl-7b-quant for now (hotpatch container image env flag USE_FUSED_KERNEL=false) and roll a canary with 2 replicas to confirm stability.

anya: agree. Who can push the hotpatch? @miguel you have the run image privileges.

miguel: prepping image tag rl-7b-hotpatch-no-fused:sha123. Plan: update deployment to 2 canary replicas in prod-usw2, wait 5m. If healthy, roll to remaining.

ops-bot: applying rollout -> `kubectl set image deploy/redwood-runtime redwood-runtime=registry/redwood/rl-7b-hotpatch-no-fused:sha123 --record`

samir: canary pods started, logs show no immediate segfaults on canary. Memory usage lower by ~22% on canary.

dev-runtime: uploading core dumps to S3 for later root-cause: s3://redwood-debug/coredumps/1769999999/*. Also capturing gdb bt from one dump:

```
#0  0x00007f9ab3c in fused_kernel::execute()
#1  0x00007f9ab4d in runtime::dispatch_forward()
#2  0x000055b3a1 in main
```

anya: good. Add to incident ticket. We should keep fallback routing until we confirm full rollback without fused kernels causes functionally equivalent outputs. Also add smoke prompts to check model output drift.

leah: note to CS: customers asked for ETA. Suggested message: "Mitigation in progress; we've routed traffic to a fallback model and applied a temporary configuration to stop crashes. Expect full restoration in 2-3 hours pending validation." Approve?

customer-success: approved message, sent.

miguel: next steps: run full canary rollout across remaining replicas with hotpatch, monitor for segfaults for 20m. If no segfaults, gradually re-enable fused-kernel with new kernel guard code (will require small code change) in next deploy.

samir: noticed two nodes had kernel oom_killer logs right before kubelet restart; filing node-level action item for infra: enable early eviction thresholds and tune GPU driver mem limit to avoid cascading OOM->segfault.

anya: assign follow-ups:
- dev-runtime: create PR with fused-kernel guard (validate memory checks) -> due EOD
- infra: tune eviction/gpu-driver config and runpostmortem -> due next day
- SRE: incident postmortem draft -> due +48h

dev-runtime: created issue RN-789 and PR draft https://git.internal/redwood/rl-runtime/pull/456 (hotpatch + guard). Will add tests.

ops-bot: status page updated -> Incident: Degraded: Some customers impacted. Mitigation: traffic rerouted to fallback. Next update in 30m.

leah: nice work. Any need to escalate to Eng oncall for kernel-level defect? @dev-runtime, is this likely a model code bug or driver/kernel bug?

dev-runtime: at first glance root cause looks like fused-kernel path not checking tensor boundary on rare long-history requests -> out-of-bounds read -> segfault after OOM-ish state. Likely a runtime bug in our kernel glue. Eng oncall should triage PR ASAP.

anya: ok escalate to eng-oncall for patch review. @miguel take lead on deploy once PR merged.

miguel: will take. Logging final status for thread: fallback routing in place, canary hotpatch healthy, nodes drained and recovering, core dumps saved, customers notified. Will keep this thread open for handoff to postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1769999999. Severity: P1 (customer-facing errors). Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-1769999999

samir: adding timeline notes to the incident doc. Last observed segfault at 14:12 UTC, traffic reroute at 14:20 UTC, hotpatch canary at 14:35 UTC.

leah: handing off to oncall for monitoring window. @samir @miguel you'll take follow-up runbooks. I'll update stakeholders.

miguel: acknowledged handoff. will monitor 2h and then start measured rollout if stable.

anya: thanks team. postmortem owners: dev-runtime (root cause + fix) and SRE (mitigation + runbook updates). Closing active pager for now. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: pager cleared by @anya at 2026-03-15T16:05:55Z.
